subject.title: fix(acpx): keep leaked non-openai model out of the Codex ACP thinking slot

question: Should OpenClaw accept `modelExplicit` and `appliedModel` as the ACP runtime boundary for distinguishing inherited defaults from explicit Codex model selections?
rationale: The patch appears correct, but it changes fallback versus fail-closed behavior and adds generic runtime contract fields that affect provider/model routing compatibility.

options.title: Accept the provenance contract
options.body: Land the PR with `modelExplicit` and `appliedModel` as the intended ACP boundary because it fixes the linked spawn regression and prevents first-turn replay of dropped defaults.

options.title: Document before merge
options.body: Ask for release-note or PR-body context that explicit unsupported Codex ACP models now fail while inherited non-OpenAI defaults are dropped.

options.title: Pause for narrower API
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want this provenance behavior expressed only inside the Codex ACP wrapper instead of the generic ACP runtime contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the provenance contract
